syllabus_topics: Introduction: Course context in current telecommunications systems, Model of a telecommunications system.
Analog modulation of sinusoidal carriers: AM, FM and PM modulation and demodulation. Bandpass signals and noise. Performance in the presence of noise.

Baseband Digital Systems: Digitization of analog sources - PCM. Sampling and Quantization. Quantization error and noise. Optimal receiver, matched filter and Inter-symbol Interference (ISI). Elementary pulse shaping (Nyquist criterion). Line codes. Eye diagram.
Bandpass Digital Systems: Motivation for digital modulation. Vector perspective. ASK, PSK and FSK systems. Multisymbol signaling (QPSK, BPSK, QAM). Detection.
Introduction to Information Theory: Quantity of information, entropy. Huffman codes, error control coding.
Introduction to optical and radio communications: Generic descriptions and performance parameters.
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 9.5 is required for the laboratory component and a minimum grade of 8 is required for the exam. For the "recourse period" (and other special periods like Worker-Students and Special Period), the final grade is calculated as 25% Laboratory (with a minimum of 9.5) and 75% Exam (with a minimum of 8). Fraudulent activities will result in the annulment of all involved assessments and will be reported to the Pedagogical Council.
